p.seg: "Tiān Guān"
King Huì of Liáng asked Wèi Liáozi,
"I have heard that the Yellow Emperor had "punishment" and "virtue"
that enabled him to win every battle.
Is this true?"
Wèi Liáozi replied,
"No,
the "punishment" and "virtue" that the Yellow Emperor spoke of
meant using "punishment" to attack
and using "virtue" to defend.
It is not what the world calls "punishment" and "virtue".
The so-called "xíng dé" (punishments and rewards) of the world,
are what the Tiānguān (officials in charge of astronomy), "shí rì" (auspicious days), "yīnyáng" (yin and yang), and "xiàngbèi" (orientation) refer to.
The Huángdì (Yellow Emperor)
is simply about human affairs.
Why?
Now, suppose there is a city here.
If you attack it from the east and west and cannot take it,
and you attack it from the north and south and cannot take it,
could it be that in all directions there are no opportunities to exploit the opportune time?
But why is it still not taken?
Because the city is tall, the moat is deep,
weapons and armor are well-prepared,
wealth and grain are abundantly stocked,
and there are worthy men unified in their plans.
But if the city walls are low, the moat is shallow, and the defenses are weak,
then it can be taken.
From this, one can see that
Tiānguān (astronomy), "shí rì" (auspicious days),
are not as important as human affairs.
According to the "Tiānguān" chapter,
"Arranging troops with their backs to water is a desperate position;
arranging troops facing a slope is a useless army."
When King Wǔ (Wǔ Wáng) attacked Zhòu,
he arrayed his troops with their backs to the Jì River and facing a mountainside slope.
He used twenty-two thousand five hundred men to defeat Zhòu's hundreds of millions and destroy the Shang Dynasty.
Could it be that Zhòu did not have knowledge of the arrangements from the Tiānguān (astronomy)?
But why was he not victorious?
Because his human affairs were not well-managed.
The Chǔ
general, Gōngzǐ Xīn, was at war with the people of Qí. At that time, a comet appeared,
with its handle pointing towards Qí.
Whichever side the handle pointed towards would be victorious,
so it could not be attacked.
Gōngzǐ Xīn said:
"What does a comet know?
To fight based on a comet
is to be certain to fall and yet win."
The next day, he fought with Qí,
and greatly defeated them.
The Yellow Emperor said:
"Before spirits and ghosts,
first examine my wisdom."
Calling it "heavenly timing"
is merely human affairs."
*Bīng Tán* (Military Discussions)
Measure the fertility of the land to establish towns and build cities.
Use cities to estimate land,
use land to estimate population,
use population to estimate grain.
If these three correspond with each other, then internally one can firmly defend,
and externally one can achieve victory in battle.
Victory in battle abroad
and preparedness for the ruler at home
must correspond with each other,
Just like matching tallies,
there is no discrepancy.
Those who manage troops,
do so as if hidden beneath the earth,
as if profound as the heavens,
arising from nothingness.
Therefore, if the barrier is closed,
even the large cannot get through,
even the small cannot expand.
Understanding clearly the prohibition, lodging, opening, and closing (of channels),
the people who are in flux will become attached to them,
and those lands that cannot bear a burden will be burdened.
If the land is wide and burdened,
then that state cannot but be wealthy;
if the people are numerous and well-governed,
then that state cannot but be well-governed.
In a wealthy and well-governed state,
the people do not set out on journeys,
and armor is not violently displayed, yet its might controls the world.
Therefore, it is said:
Victory in war is won in the court.
To win without displaying armor violently
is the ruler’s victory;
to win after deploying troops
is the general’s victory.
War should not be initiated out of anger,
Seeing victory, then advance;
not seeing victory, then halt.
If the trouble is within a hundred *lǐ*,
do not mobilize troops for even a single day;
if the trouble is within a thousand *lǐ*,
do not mobilize troops for even a month;
if the trouble is within the four seas,
do not mobilize troops for even a year.
A general, above, is not controlled by Heaven;
below, is not controlled by Earth;
in the middle, is not controlled by people.
One who is generous cannot be provoked to anger;
one who is incorruptible cannot be swayed by wealth.
Truly, one who is mad at heart, blind in sight, and deaf in hearing,
and leads others with these three perversities, is in dire straits.
Wherever the army reaches,
even a narrow path like a sheep's intestine can be conquered,
even a serrated ridge can be conquered;
following the mountain can be conquered,
entering the valley can be conquered;
a square formation can be conquered,
a round formation can be conquered.
When heavy, be like mountains, like forests,
like rivers, like great rivers;
when light, be like cannon fire, like scorching flames,
like leaks, like collapses,
like a wall crushing down,
Like clouds and rainbows covering them,
causing them to gather and be unable to disperse,
to disperse and be unable to gather;
to go left and be unable to go right,
to go right and be unable to go left.
The soldiers are like a bundle of wood,
the crossbows are like sheep horns,
everyone is without exception leaping and raising their courage,
cutting off all doubts and worries,
resolutely and grandly going forth.
*Zhì Tán* ("Control Discourses")
In all military systems, it is necessary to first establish a control.
If the control is established first, then the soldiers will not be in disorder,
if the soldiers are not in disorder, then the punishments will be clear.
Where the gongs and drums point,
then a hundred men will all fight;
if they fall into formations and disrupt the lines,
then a thousand men will all fight;
if they overturn the army and kill the generals,
then ten thousand men will all wield their blades together,
and in all under Heaven, none will be able to withstand their battle.
In ancient times, soldiers were organized in units of ten and five,
chariots had side formations.
When the drums sound and the flags wave,
those who were the first to climb the walls were never not strong national warriors,
those who died first were also never not strong national warriors.
To lose one enemy soldier while losing a hundred of our own,
this enriches the enemy and harms us greatly,
and a worldly general will be unable to prevent it.
If soldiers conscripted for service desert and return home,
or flee north even at the point of battle,
then the desertion and casualties are severe,
and a worldly general will be unable to prevent it.
That which kills a person from a hundred paces away
is the bow and arrow.
That which kills a person from within fifty paces
is the spear and halberd.
If after the general has sounded the drum, the soldiers are noisy and riotous with each other,
breaking arrows, snapping spears, and embracing halberds for the advantage of firing last.
If such things as these occur in battle,
it is internal self-defeat,
and a worldly general will be unable to prevent it.
If soldiers lose their squads,
chariots lose their formations,
surprise troops abandon their general and flee,
and the main body also flees,
a worldly general will be unable to prevent it.
If a general can prevent these four things,
then he can make a high mountain a plain,
turn a deep river into a shallow one,
and assault a strong formation.
If he cannot prevent these four things,
it is like losing boat and oars while crossing a river,
an impossibility.
It is not that the people enjoy death and dislike life;
when orders are clear,
and laws and regulations are carefully enforced,
then they can be made to advance.
Clearly reward in the front,
and decisively punish in the rear,
therefore, launches are able to hit the target,
and actions then have merit.
Now, one squad leader *zú* for every hundred people,
one *Sīmǎ* for every thousand people,
and one general *jiàng* for every ten thousand people;
with the few suppressing the many,
with the weak suppressing the strong.
Try listening to your servant explain the method;
it can make the troops of the entire army
punish a single villain
without misapplying the law;
fathers will not dare to protect their sons,
and sons will not dare to protect their fathers,
let alone the people of the country.
If a single bandit attacks in the marketplace with a sword,
ten thousand people will invariably avoid him.
Your servant says that it is not that the single bandit is particularly brave
or that ten thousand people are all worthless.
Why?
Certain death and certain life
Gù bù móu yě. Indeed, they are not comparable.
Tīng chén zhī shù, Listen to my methods,
zú shǐ sān jūn zhī zhòng wèi yī sǐ zéi, it is sufficient to make the masses of the three armies into a death-defying force,
mò dāng qí qián, none can withstand them in front,
mò suí qí hòu, none can follow them from behind,
ér néng dú chū dú rù yān. and they can independently sally forth and return.
Dú chū dú rù zhě, Those who can independently sally forth and return,
wáng bà zhī bīng yě. are the troops of a true king or hegemon.
Yǒu tí shí wàn zhī zhòng ér tiānxià mò dāng zhě, Is there someone who, leading a force of 100,000, could not be matched by anyone in the world?
shéi? Who?
Yuē: The answer is:
Huán Gōng yě. Duke Huán.
Yǒu tí qī wàn zhī zhòng ér tiānxià mò dāng zhě, Is there someone who, leading a force of 70,000, could not be matched by anyone in the world?
shéi? Who?
Yuē: The answer is:
Wú Qǐ yě. Wú Qǐ.
Yǒu tí sān wàn zhī zhòng ér tiānxià mò dāng zhě, Is there someone who, leading a force of 30,000, could not be matched by anyone in the world?
shéi? Who?
Yuē: The answer is:
Wǔ Zǐ yě. Wǔ Zǐ.
Jīn tiānxià zhū guó shì, Now, the leaders of the various states in the world,
suǒ shuài wú bù jí èrshí wàn zhī zhòng, all command no fewer than 200,000 troops,
rán bù néng jì gōngmíng zhě, but are unable to achieve fame and success,
bù míng hū jìn shě kāisāi yě. because they do not understand the principles of prohibitions, allowances, openings, and blockages.
Míng qí zhì, If one understands these principles,
yī rén shèng zhī, then one person can overcome them,
zé shí rén yì yǐ shèng zhī yě; and so ten people can also overcome them;
If you can defeat ten men,
then you can defeat a hundred, a thousand, even ten thousand men.
Therefore it is said:
make convenient our weapons and tools,
nurture our martial valor,
and unleash it like a bird striking,
like rushing into a thousand-fathom ravine.
Now, when a state is afflicted,
it sends out valuable treasures as gifts,
it sends out beloved sons as hostages,
it cedes territory,
and obtains auxiliary soldiers from the world.
They are nominally said to be a hundred thousand,
but in reality, they are no more than several tens of thousands.
When their soldiers come,
none of them fail to say to their general:
"Do not be the first to fight in the world."
In reality, they cannot be obtained and fought with.
Consider the people within our borders;
there is no group of five that cannot be governed correctly.
If you regulate a hundred thousand troops,
and the king can certainly make them wear our clothes,
eat our food,
and if they do not win in battle,
and do not hold firm in defense,
it is not the fault of our people,
It originates from within.
If all the states under Heaven help me in battle,
it would be like the swiftness of excellent steeds like Lù Ěr (騄耳) and Jì (驥);
those inferior horses raising their manes in rivalry,
how could they possibly inherit my spirit!
I use the resources of all under Heaven as my resources,
I make the laws of all under Heaven my laws.
I cultivate my commands and decrees,
I clarify my punishments and rewards,
making it so that no one under Heaven can obtain food if they do not farm,
and no one can obtain rank if they do not fight.
Make the people raise their arms vying to engage in farming and war, and then the world will be without equal.
Therefore it is said:
"Issue commands and decrees,
and ensure they are faithfully implemented within the country."
If the people say they have a plan to defeat the enemy,
do not permit their empty words,
but certainly test their ability to fight.
Observing another's land and possessing it,
dividing another's people and raising them,
certainly allows one to have their worthy men within.
To want to possess the world without being able to have worthy men within,
will surely result in the destruction of armies and the death of generals.
Like this,
even if victorious in battle, the state grows weaker;
even if acquiring land, the state grows poorer,
The flaws of the state's domestic system are already apparent.
*Zhàn Wēi* (Battle Majesty)
In general, there are those who win with *dào* (道, principle),
those who win with *wēi* (威, majesty),
and those who win with *lì* (力, strength).
Through military exercises and assessing the enemy,
causing the enemy's spirit to be lost and their armies scattered,
even if their formation remains intact, it cannot be used.
This is winning with *dào*.
By carefully examining laws and regulations,
clearly defining rewards and punishments,
and making equipment convenient to use,
the people will have a firm resolve to fight.
This is winning with *wēi*.
Breaking enemy ranks and killing their generals,
using mobile weaponry and seizing fortifications,
routing the masses and capturing territory,
returning only after achieving success,
This is winning with *lì*.
If a king or lord knows how to win by these three means,
everything will be accomplished.
The people are the reason why generals and soldiers fight;
people fight because of
their *qì* (氣, vital energy/spirit).
When *qì* is strong, they fight;
when *qì* is weakened, they flee.
If morale is seized, they will flee.
It is like punishments have not yet been applied,
and soldiers have not yet engaged, but there are five ways to seize the enemy:
first is the discussion of victory in the ancestral temple;
second is the discussion of receiving orders;
third is the discussion of crossing borders;
fourth is the discussion of deep trenches and high ramparts;
fifth is the discussion of arraying formations and adding punishments.
These five,
first assess the enemy and then act,
therefore, attacking the void seizes them.
Those skilled in using soldiers
are able to seize others but not be seized by others.
Seizing is the mechanism of the mind.
Orders are that by which the minds of the masses are unified.
If the masses are not discerning, then plans change frequently;
if plans change frequently, then even if orders are issued,
the masses will not believe them.
Therefore, the principle of orders is
even if there is a small mistake, do not change it;
if there is a small doubt, do not elaborate.
This is how matters rely on the strength of the masses.
If what is being undertaken is not assessed, then plans change frequently;
if plans change frequently, then even if matters begin,
the masses will not be at peace.
The principle of undertaking matters is
even if there is a small mistake, do not change it;
Minor difficulties do not cause distress.
Therefore, if the ruler issues commands without doubt,
then the people will not listen with divided attention.
If actions are undertaken without doubtful matters,
then the people will not have divided wills.
In ancient times, those who led the people,
none of them could gain their strength without trusting their hearts,
and none of them could achieve their desperate fighting without obtaining their strength.
Therefore, a state must possess the principles of propriety, trustworthiness, affection, and love,
then it can exchange hunger for satiety.
A state must possess customs of filial piety, compassion, integrity, and a sense of shame,
then it can exchange death for life.
In ancient times, leading the people,
one must first prioritize propriety and trustworthiness, then ranks and emoluments;
first integrity and a sense of shame, then punishments;
first affection and love, then regulate their conduct.
Therefore, warfare
must be rooted in leading oneself to encourage the troops,
just as the heart directs the four limbs.
If the will is not encouraged,
then the soldiers will not die for their principles.
If the soldiers do not die for their principles,
then the masses will not fight.
The way to encourage the soldiers,
the means by which the people live,
cannot be treated lightly.
The levels of ranks and titles,
the familial relations in death and mourning,
and what the people strive for
must be made clear.
It is essential to establish them based on what the people produce
and to make them prominent based on what the people honor.
The reality of land stipends (tián lù),
the grain for food and drink,
relatives and fellow villagers,
mutual encouragement within the village,
mutual assistance in life and death,
mutual following in military service—
these are what motivate the people.
Make the units of ten and five (shí wǔ) like relatives,
and the leaders of a hundred (zú bó) like friends;
therefore, when the soldiers stop, they are like a wall,
and when they move, they are like wind and rain.
The chariots do not form tangled tracks,
and the soldiers do not turn their heels.
This is the fundamental principle of warfare.
Land is what nourishes the people,
walls are what defend the land,
and warfare is what defends the walls.
Therefore, if they devote themselves to farming, the people will not be hungry;
if they devote themselves to defense, their land will not be in danger;
if they devote themselves to warfare, their cities will not be besieged.
These three are the fundamental tasks of the former kings,
Běn wù zhě, bīng zuì jí.
Therefore, the former kings focused on the military.
Focusing on the military
has five fundamentals:
If supplies are insufficient,
then the soldiers will not advance;
if rewards and emoluments are not generous,
then the people will not be encouraged;
if martial men are not selected,
then the troops will not be strong;
if preparations are not convenient,
then strength will not be robust;
if punishments and rewards are not appropriate,
then the troops will not be awed.
The former kings focused on these five things,
therefore, in stillness, they could defend what was secure,
and in action, they could achieve what they desired.
Now, using the defensive to launch an offensive
means the defensive positions should be strong,
the formations should be firm,
the attacks should be complete,
and the fighting should be coordinated.
A kingdom that aspires to be a true kingdom enriches its people,
a hegemonic kingdom enriches its warriors,
a barely surviving kingdom enriches its high officials,
and a doomed kingdom enriches its granaries.
The so-called "overflowing above and leaking below"
is a disaster that cannot be remedied.
Therefore, it is said:
"Promote the worthy and employ the capable,"
and affairs will be beneficial without choosing a date;
"Make laws clear and scrutinize orders,"
and affairs will be auspicious without divination;
"Value merit and provide for the weary,"
and blessings will be obtained without praying to spirits.
It is also said:
"The timing of Heaven is not as good as the advantages of the Earth,"
"and the advantages of the Earth are not as good as the harmony of the People."
What the sage values
is nothing more than human affairs.
As for a diligent and hardworking army,
the general will not put himself first:
in the heat, he does not raise a canopy;
in the cold, he does not wear extra clothes;
when there are dangerous ascents and descents,
the general will surely dismount and walk;
he drinks only after the army's well is completed;
he eats only after the army's food is cooked;
he rests only after the army's camp is built;
if the army has not finished eating,
he also does not light a fire for food.
He shares hunger, satiety, weariness, ease, cold, and heat with them personally.
Thus,
the army, though long-standing, will not become senile,
and though senile, will not be corrupt.
*Gōng Quán* (Attacking Authority):
An army prevails through stillness,
a state prevails through focus.
Those whose strength is divided are weak,
those whose hearts are doubtful betray.
For when strength is weak, advancement and retreat lack heroism,
and enemies are let go without being captured.
Generals, officers, soldiers—
their movements and stillness are of one body.
Once the heart is doubtful and betrayed,
plans are decided upon but not acted upon,
actions are decided upon but not controlled.
When different mouths utter false words,
the general will lack a dignified appearance,
the soldiers will lack constant training,
and every attack launched will be defeated.
This is called an army of eroding hills,
and is not worth fighting against.
The general is the heart,
and the subordinates are the limbs.
If the heart moves with sincerity,
then the limbs will surely exert strength;
if the heart moves with doubt,
then the limbs will surely betray.
Now, if a general's heart does not control [his troops],
and soldiers' movements are not disciplined,
even if they win,
it is a lucky victory,
not the result of strategic planning.
Now, the people should not have two fears.
They should fear our insulting the enemy
and fear the enemy insulting us.
Those who are seen as insulted will be defeated,
those who establish authority will be victorious.
In general, those who understand the principle:
officials will fear their generals;
if officials fear their generals,
the people will fear the officials;
if the people fear the officials,
the enemy will fear the people.
Therefore, those who know the way to victory and defeat
must first know the balance of fear and insult.
Now, those who do not love and persuade others' hearts
will not be employed by me;
those who do not strictly command reverence in others' hearts
will not be promoted by me.
Love causes those below to be compliant,
authority causes those above to be established;
love ensures no disloyalty,
authority ensures no transgression.
Thus, a good general
relies solely on love and authority.
If a battle's victory is not assured,
one should not speak of battle;
if a siege's success is not assured,
one should not speak of siege.
Otherwise,
even punishments and rewards will lack credibility.
Credibility must be established before the appointed time,
and preparations must be made before any signs appear.
Therefore, once the troops have gathered, they should not be dispersed in vain;
once the army has marched out, it should not return without purpose.
Seek the enemy as if searching for a lost child,
strike the enemy as if rescuing a drowning person.
Those who divide their forces at dangerous locations lack the will to fight;
those who issue challenges lack complete morale;
those who engage in duels have no victorious soldiers.
Generally, those who fight in the name of righteousness
value having the initiative originate from themselves;
those who fight over personal grievances
are only acting out of necessity.
Even if grudges have already formed,
it is best to address them later.
Therefore, one must definitely wait when contending,
and one must definitely prepare during respite.
In warfare, there are victories achieved at the court,
victories achieved in the open country,
and victories achieved in the marketplace.
Fight and you gain;
submit and you lose.
To be fortunate enough to merely avoid defeat
is to achieve a partial victory through the enemy's unexpected surprise and fear.
"Partial victory"
means not a complete victory.
Those who do not achieve complete victory have no authority or reputation.
Therefore, when an enlightened ruler wages war,
drums and horns are sounded in unison,
regulated with weapons.
He does not seek victory, but achieves it nonetheless.
There are those who achieve victory by eliminating preparations and dismantling displays of power,
because they have established laws.
Their weaponry is determined early on.
Their response to the enemy is comprehensive;
their command is absolute.
Therefore, five men form a wǔ (伍),
ten men form a shí (什),
one hundred men form a zú (卒),
one thousand men form a shuài (率),
and ten thousand men form a jiàng (將).
Everything is comprehensive and absolute.
If someone dies in the morning, they are replaced in the morning;
if someone dies in the evening, they are replaced in the evening.
Weigh the enemy, examine the generals, and then raise troops.
Therefore, whenever assembling troops,
those from a thousand *lǐ* take ten days,
those from a hundred *lǐ* take one day;
you must assemble within the enemy's territory.
Once the soldiers are gathered and the generals have arrived,
deeply penetrate their land,
sever their routes,
and encamp near their large cities and towns.
Force them to ascend the city walls under imminent threat,
men and women in multiple layers,
each exploiting the terrain to attack key fortresses.
Occupy one city or town and cut off several roads,
and then attack it.
If the enemy generals and commanders cannot trust each other,
if the officials and soldiers cannot harmonize,
and if there are those who do not follow the laws,
then we will defeat them.
Before enemy reinforcements arrive,
one city will already have surrendered.
If the ferries and bridges have not been prepared,
the key fortresses have not been repaired,
the city defenses have not been established,
and the moats and barricades have not been set up,
then even though there is a city, there is no defense.
If the distant outposts have not been manned,
When soldiers on the frontier have not returned,
then even though there are people, it is as if there are none.
When the six domestic animals are not gathered,
the five grains are not harvested,
and wealth and resources are not collected,
then even though there are assets, it is as if there are none.
Now, a city that is empty and whose resources are exhausted,
I take advantage of its emptiness to attack it.
The *Fa* (law, method) says:
"Go out alone, come in alone;
the enemy does not engage in close combat but brings it about."
This is what it means.
*Shǒu Quán* (Holding Authority)
In general, those who defend,
advancing without outer walls or barriers, retreating without pavilions or fortifications to resist the battle,
are not the best.
Heroes and outstanding men,
strong armor and sharp weapons,
powerful crossbows and strong arrows,
all are within the outer walls.
Then, they gather up stores and granaries,
destroy and break them to enter and defend.
Causing the invading force's morale to be a hundredfold,
while the defender's morale is not even half,
those who attack the enemy, injure them severely.
However, the generals of the world are unable to understand this.
Now, a defender is one who does not lose the advantage of their strategic position.
The method of defense is:
For every one *zhàng* of city wall,
ten men should defend it,
with the labor force's food not included in this calculation.
Those who go out do not defend;
those who defend do not go out.
One man should be able to hold against ten,
ten against a hundred,
a hundred against a thousand,
a thousand against ten thousand.
Therefore, building city walls
is not a wasteful expenditure of the people's efforts in piling up earth,
but is truly for the purpose of defense.
A city wall of a thousand *zhàng*
requires ten thousand men to defend it.
If the moat is deep and wide,
the city wall is solid and thick,
the soldiers and people are well-prepared,
firewood and food are plentiful,
crossbows are strong and arrows powerful,
spears and halberds are suitable in number,
this is the method of defense.
If the attacker does not have a force of over a hundred thousand,
and if there is an army that will surely come to its rescue,
then there is a city that must be defended.
If there is no army that will certainly come to the rescue,
then there is no city that will certainly be defended.
If the city is strong and the rescue is sincere,
then even foolish men and ignorant women will not fail to protect the city, using all their resources and blood to defend it.
For a city that can be held for a year,
defense will be more than enough to counter the attack,
and rescue will be more than enough to support the defense.
If the city is strong but the rescue is not sincere,
then even foolish men and ignorant women will do nothing but weep on the battlements;
this is the normal human emotion.
Even if you then open the granaries and provide relief,
it still cannot be stopped.
You must rouse the heroes and valiant men,
with strong armor and sharp weapons,
and strong crossbows and powerful arrows arrayed at the front,
with the small and emaciated arrayed at the rear.
If a hundred thousand troops are encamped under the city,
the rescuers must open the way,
and the defenders must come out.
Come out and occupy strategic points,
only supporting them from behind,
without cutting off their supply lines,
so that the interior and exterior correspond to each other.
This is rescuing while showing insincerity;
showing insincerity means to topple the enemy and wait for them.
Put the strong behind,
and the old in front;
If the enemy is invincible,
defense cannot be sustained.
This is called the expedient of defense.
*Shí'èr Líng* [Twelve Mausoleums]
Authority lies in immutability.
Kindness lies in adapting to the times.
Opportunity lies in responding to events.
Victory in battle lies in regulating morale.
Attack lies in exceeding expectations.

The *jiǎo* (角) note is the *shuài gǔ* (帥鼓, commander's drum);
it is the commander's drum.
The small drum is the *bó gǔ* (伯鼓, leader's drum);
it is the leader's drum.
When the three drums sound in unison,
then the general, commander, and leader
are of one mind.
A surprise attack is the opposite of this.
Those whose drumming is out of order will be punished;
those who are noisy and clamorous will be punished;
those who move without heeding the gong, drum, bell, or flags will be punished.
Teach one hundred men to fight,
when they are trained, combine them into one thousand men.
When one thousand men are trained,
combine them into ten thousand men.
Having taught and trained ten thousand men,
assemble them within the three armies.
The multitude of the three armies
has divisions and combinations,
forming the methods of great battles,
teaching them to success and testing them with reviews.
The square formation also wins,
the round formation also wins;
the staggered and oblique formation also wins,
facing danger also wins.
If the enemy is in the mountains,
follow them along the slopes;
if the enemy is in the deep waters,
submerge and follow them.
Seek the enemy as if seeking a lost son,
follow them without doubt,
therefore you can defeat the enemy and control their fate.
For early decisions precede the enemy.
If plans are not determined beforehand,
and considerations are not decided early,
then advance and retreat are uncertain,
and doubt arises, leading to certain defeat.
Therefore, regular forces value being first,
while surprise forces value being last;
sometimes first, sometimes last,
this is how to control the enemy.
If a general does not understand the law,
acts on his own authority,
attacks rashly and is brave,
there is none who will not be defeated.
If his actions are doubtful yet he does not doubt,
if his advances are based on trust yet he does not trust,
if his deliveries are sometimes slow and sometimes fast, and sometimes neither,
these three things
are a hindrance to battle.
*Jiàng Lìng* ("General's Orders")
When a general receives orders,
the ruler must first deliberate in the ancestral temple,
and issue commands in the court.
The ruler personally hands the general an ax, saying:
"The left, right, and central armies
all have assigned duties.
If anyone exceeds their duty and seeks instructions from above, they shall be put to death.
The army shall have no second command.
Those who give a second command shall be executed;
those who withhold a command shall be executed;
those who fail to execute a command shall be executed."
The general announces:
"Once outside the gates of the country,
a time will be set for noon.
Campsites will be designated, and the gate of the camp will be established by that time;
If they are late, they will be punished according to the law."
When the general enters the camp,
he immediately closes the gates and clears the roads.
Anyone who dares to walk on them will be executed.
Anyone who dares to speak loudly will be executed.
Anyone who dares to disobey orders will be executed.
*Zhǒng Jūnlìng* ("Regulations for the Rear Army")
What is meant by the "rear army" (*zhǒng jūn*)
is to be one hundred *lǐ* away from the main army,
with a set meeting place,
preparing cooked food for three days,
and marching ahead of the front army.
They prepare signals for battle engagement;
the engagement signals are then raised.
The rear army feasts the soldiers
and makes them prepare for battle formations;
this is what is meant by those who hasten to battle.
As for the "arising army" (*xīng jūn*),
they march ahead of the rear army,
and the engagement signals are then raised.
They are twice the distance from the main army,
one hundred *lǐ* away from the rear army,
with a set meeting place,
preparing cooked food for six days,
and preparing for battle.
They divide soldiers to occupy strategic locations.
If victorious in battle, then pursue the defeated;
hold back the troops and advance towards them.
If following the army one encounters those returning (deserting),
execute them.
What is meant by the armies of the various generals
being victorious when within the *sì qí* 四奇 (four strategic deployments).
An army has groups of ten and five,
there is division and combination.
Establish their duties beforehand,
guarding important passes and bridges and dwelling separately.
When the signal for battle is raised,
they should all assemble.
The main army should calculate the food needed on a daily basis,
and preparations for battle must be complete.
If orders are carried out and action is taken,
those who do not follow orders will be executed.
Generally, those who are called to divide and defend the passes
within the four borders,
when the army that initiates the campaign and the army that follows have set out,
then the people within the four borders
must not be allowed to travel.
Receiving the king's command,
holding the bestowed tally as proof,
they are called officials with *shùn zhí* 順職 (designated responsibilities);
those who are not officials with *shùn zhí* 順職 (designated responsibilities) but travel,
will be executed.
When the records of battles and alliances arise,
officials who follow their duties accordingly act,
using these records to cross-reference.
Therefore, if one desires to wage war,
first one must secure the internal affairs.
*Bīng Jiào Shàng* (On Military Education, Part 1)
In the military's instructions and commands,
dividing camps and arranging formations,
those who advance or retreat without orders
shall be punished with the crime of violating instructions.
Those who move forward shall be instructed on moving forward,
those who move backward shall be instructed on moving backward;
those who move to the left shall be instructed on moving to the left,
those who move to the right shall be instructed on moving to the right.
If instruction is carried out among five men,
their company leader shall receive a reward;
if they are not instructed,
it is as if they have committed the crime of violating instructions.
Those who desert their position shall be reported by their squad,
within the squad they shall report on each other to
avoid punishment.
Whenever a squad faces the battle formation,
if even one person fails to advance and dies at the hands of the enemy,
then the instructor shall be punished as if he were a lawbreaker.
Whenever a group of ten guarantees each other's safety,
if one person flees and the other nine do not all die fighting the enemy,
then the instructor shall be punished as if they committed the crime.
From the group of ten upwards to the assistant general, if there is anyone who does not follow the law,
then the instructor shall be punished as if they committed the crime.
In all cases, clarifying penalties,
correctly encouraging rewards,
must be based on the methods of military instruction.
The general's flag is different,
the soldiers' badges are different.
The left army's badge is on the left shoulder,
the right army's badge is on the right shoulder,
the central army's badge is on the chest.
On the badge is written:
"So-and-so, soldier of such-and-such."
The badges are arranged in five ranks, front and back.
The most respected badge is placed at the top,
and the others are placed in descending order of importance.
The squad leader (Wǔzhǎng) instructs his four men,
using a board as a drum,
using a tile as a gong,
using a pole as a flag.
Strike the drum to advance,
lower the flag to hasten,
strike the gong to retreat;
wave [the flag] to go left,
wave [the flag] to go right;
strike both gong and drum to sit down.
The Wǔzhǎng (伍長) trains them and completes their training,
then combines them into a Shízhǎng's (什長) squad.
The Shízhǎng (什長) trains them and completes their training,
then combines them into a Zúzhang's (卒長) platoon.
The Zúzhang (卒長) trains them and completes their training,
then combines them into a Bózhǎng's (伯長) company.
The Bózhǎng (伯長) trains them and completes their training,
then combines them into a Bīngwèi's (兵尉) command.
The Bīngwèi (兵尉) trains them and completes their training,
then combines them into a Píjiàng's (裨將) division.
The Píjiàng (裨將) trains them and completes their training,
then combines them into a Dàjiàng's (大將) army.
The Dàjiàng (大將) trains them,
and arrays them in the open field.
Set up large markers,
one every three hundred paces.
Once the formation is set and the markers are removed,
decide the course every hundred paces,
advance briskly every hundred paces,
and gallop every hundred paces.
Practice combat to perfect their discipline,
and then establish reward methods for them.
From the Wèi (尉) officers and below, all should have flags.
Those who capture flags in battle
will be rewarded according to the rank they have achieved,
in order to clarify the intention of reward and encouragement.
Victory lies in establishing authority;
Establishing authority lies in united strength;
United strength lies in just rewards and punishments.
Just rewards and punishments
are the means to clarify rewards.
To cause the people to disregard the borders of the country,
to decide the line between life and death,
and to teach them to die without doubt,
there is a reason for this.
To make those who defend, defend firmly,
and those who fight, fight fiercely;
to prevent treacherous schemes from arising,
and treacherous people from speaking;
to make orders executed without change,
and troops move without suspicion;
swift as thunder,
to rouse the enemy as if startled;
to recognize merit and distinguish virtue,
as clearly as black and white;
to make the people follow the commands of their superiors
as readily as the four limbs respond to the mind.
That the front army can cut through formations, disrupt ranks, and shatter strongholds as if collapsing
there is a reason for this.
This is what is called military instruction,
the means to open up territories,
protect the state,
To eliminate calamities and harm,
and to establish martial virtue.
"Military Instruction Below"
Your servant has heard that a ruler possesses a way to certain victory,
and thus is able to annex and expand greatly,
unifying the system and regulations,
so that his authority extends throughout the realm, and there are twelve [methods]:
First is joint punishment (lián xíng),
referring to joint responsibility for the same crime among groups;
second is territorial restriction (dì jìn),
referring to prohibiting passage,
to ensnare external transgressions;
third is complete chariot (quán chē),
referring to the armor and the head being attached,
groups of three or five being identical,
to solidify their connection;
fourth is opening and closing (kāi sāi),
referring to dividing territory with boundaries,
each devoted to their duty and firmly defending;
fifth is dividing boundaries (fēn xiàn),
referring to the left and right mutually restricting,
the front and rear mutually supporting,
chariots forming a defensive wall,
to oppose and halt [the enemy];
sixth is distinct commands (hào bié),
referring to the front ranks striving to advance,
to distinguish them from those behind,
The seventh is called "Five Orders,"
meaning to make the ranks and files clear,
so that the beginning and the end are not confused.
The eighth is called "Complete Curves,"
meaning that the curves follow each other,
with each having its own assigned section.
The ninth is called "Metal and Drums,"
meaning to reward merit and
honor virtue.
The tenth is called "Arrayed Chariots,"
meaning to connect the spears in front,
with horses risking their eyes.
The eleventh is called "Dare-to-Die Soldiers,"
meaning those with talent and strength among the troops,
who ride in war chariots,
moving vertically and horizontally,
to surprise and subdue the enemy.
The twelfth is called "Strong Soldiers,"
meaning they pass through the flags and complete curves,
and do not move without being commanded.
When these twelve are taught and perfected,
violations of orders will not be tolerated.
They can make a weak army strong,
they can make a lowly ruler esteemed,
they can revive declining orders,
they can make scattered people intimate,
With a large population, one can govern;
with vast territory, one can defend.
The state's chariots do not leave the inner gate,
and armored troops do not come out of their cases, yet (the state's) majesty subdues the world.
There are five essentials for soldiers:
as a general, forgetting the family;
crossing the border, forgetting relatives;
pointing at the enemy, forgetting oneself;
being certain to die leads to survival;
eagerly pursuing victory is the inferior way.
If a hundred men are exposed to blades,
they will become mired, scattering the battle array;
if a thousand men are exposed to blades,
they will capture enemies and kill generals;
if ten thousand men are exposed to blades,
they will move unhindered throughout the world.
King Wǔ asked Tàigōng Wàng, saying:
"I wish to briefly discuss the essentials of employing men to the utmost."
Wàng answered, saying:
"Rewards should be like mountains,
punishments like streams.
The best have no faults,
the next best correct faults,
so that people cannot have private conversations.
Those who plead against punishments should die;
those who plead against rewards should die."
To attack a state, one must take advantage of its internal changes.
Tempt them with wealth to observe their poverty;
Reveal their shortcomings to observe their weaknesses;
When superiors are discordant, inferiors will become estranged.
Things like these
are causes for attacking them.
Now, during the Warring States period, the states attacked each other;
great attacks were made on those with virtue,
from groups of five to pairs,
from pairs to armies,
without unified commands.
Leading to the populace's hearts being unsettled,
merely valuing arrogance and extravagance,
plotting calamity and arguing disputes,
with officials investigating their affairs,
accumulating (problems) and leading to defeat.
As the day ends and the road is long,
there will still be those whose morale is diminished;
when the army is old and the general is greedy,
competing to plunder, they are easily defeated.
Generally, when the general is reckless, the ramparts are low, and the masses are agitated,
they are vulnerable to attack;
when the general is prudent, the ramparts are high, and the masses are fearful,
they are vulnerable to being besieged.
In general, when besieging, one must offer small advantages,
causing them to gradually weaken and become feeble,
then being stingy, there will be those who go without food.
When the masses attack at night,
it is out of fear;
when the masses avoid duties,
it is out of discord.
Relying on others to save them,
To anticipate battle and be apprehensive,
is all a matter of losing heart and injuring one’s morale.
Injured morale leads to defeated armies,
crooked schemes lead to ruined states.
"On Military Commands"
In general, when raising an army, one must carefully assess the power within and without,
and plan accordingly before acting.
Observe whether the army is prepared or lacking,
whether food supplies are abundant or insufficient.
Assess the entry and exit routes.
Then, raising an army to attack the disordered will
surely be able to penetrate them.
If the territory is large but the cities are small,
then first seize their territory;
if the cities are large but the territory is narrow,
then first attack their cities;
if the territory is vast but the population is sparse,
then cut off their strategic passes;
if the territory is narrow but the population is dense,
then build large mounds to overlook them.
Do not lose their benefits,
do not seize their time,
relax their government,
level their industries,
remedy their flaws,
then it will be enough to implement across the world.
Weapons are instruments of ill omen;
warfare is contrary to virtue;
affairs must have a basis,
therefore, a true king attacks violence and disorder based on benevolence and righteousness.
During the Warring States period, arms were employed to establish authority, resist enemies, and scheme against each other, making it impossible to abolish warfare.
Military affairs take martial prowess as their foundation,
and culture as their seed;
martial prowess as the exterior,
and culture as the interior;
martial prowess as the outside,
and culture as the inside;
if one can carefully examine these three aspects,
then one will understand the reasons for victory and defeat.
Culture is used to discern profits and losses, and to distinguish safety from danger;
martial prowess is used to assault strong enemies, and to vigorously attack and defend.
The application of military force involves both culture and martial prowess;
it is like an echo responding to a sound,
like a shadow following a body.
Focused unity leads to victory,
disunity leads to defeat;
formations that are dense are firm,
The army's edge (fēng) is effective when dispersed.
If a general has authority, then [his army] will thrive;
without authority, [it] will perish.
With authority, [he] will be victorious;
without authority, [he] will be defeated.
If soldiers have a general, they will fight;
without a general, they will flee in defeat.
With a general, they will die for their cause;
without a general, they will suffer humiliation.
Authority (wēi) refers to rewards and punishments.
If the soldiers fear their general more than the enemy, they will be victorious;
if the soldiers fear the enemy more than their general, they will be defeated.
The way to know victory or defeat
is by how the soldiers view their general compared to the enemy.
The enemy and the general are like the pans of a scale;
stability leads to order,
rash action leads to chaos.
In deploying soldiers and arraying troops, there are established orders;
in the spacing and arrangement of ranks, there are established methods;
in the order of advance and retreat, there is what is appropriate.
These established orders
are not for pursuing defeated enemies or attacking fortified towns.
If the order of advance and retreat is not maintained, there will be mistakes;
those who disrupt the order of advance and retreat will be executed.
Regular formations all face the enemy,
some facing inward,
some facing outward;
There is a standing battle formation,
there is a seated battle formation.
The inward-facing formation is for guarding the center,
the outward-facing formation is for preparing against the outside.
The standing formation is for moving,
the seated formation is for stopping.
The standing and seated battle formations,
advancing and stopping in coordination,
the general is within them.
For the seated formation, use swords and axes;
for the standing formation, use halberds and crossbows;
the general also resides in the center.
One who is good at defending against the enemy,
first engages with the main force,
and then seizes the strategic points.
This is a certain victory tactic.
Axes and battle-axes in the battle formation,
adorn it with flags and banners;
those who have merit will certainly be rewarded,
those who violate orders will certainly be put to death.
Survival and death,
depend on the end of the drumstick.
Even if there are skilled soldiers in the world,
none can resist this.
Before arrows are shot and exchanged,
before long blades are engaged,
Those who clamor in front are called *xū* (虛, empty),
those who clamor behind are called *shí* (實, full),
and those who do not clamor are called *bì* (祕, secret).
*Xū* and *shí*
are the essence of military affairs.
*Bīng Lìng Xià* (兵令下, Military Orders Below)
Regarding those who leave the main army to prepare for defense in front,
the border counties and marquises
should be spaced three to five *lǐ* apart.
Upon hearing that the main army is preparing for defense in front,
all fighting is prohibited,
to ensure internal security.
When internal soldiers are sent to garrison,
order the officers to issue flags, drums, *gē* (戈, halberd) and armor.
On the day of departure,
any officers who arrive after the departure date or after crossing the county boundary
will be punished according to the law for late arrival to garrison duty.
If a soldier garrisoning the border for one year deserts without waiting for a replacement,
the punishment will be the same as for deserting from the army.
If the parents, wife, and children know about it,
they will be punished with the same crime;
if they do not know,
they will be pardoned.
If a soldier arrives at the general's location one day later than the officer,
the parents, wife, and children will all be punished with the same crime.
If a soldier escapes home and arrives one day later,
If the parents, wives, and children do not arrest or report (criminals),
they shall also be guilty of the same crime.
Those who lose their generals and officers in battle,
and those generals and officers who abandon their soldiers and retreat alone,
shall all be beheaded.
If a former officer abandons his soldiers and retreats,
and a subsequent officer is able to behead him and recover his soldiers, he shall be rewarded.
Those in the army who have no merit shall be sent to garrison for three years.
In a major battle of the three armies,
if the great general dies,
and more than five hundred subordinate officials do not die fighting the enemy, they shall be beheaded;
all of the great general's close soldiers on the battle line shall be beheaded;
the remaining soldiers who have military merit shall have one rank taken away,
and those who have no military merit shall be sent to garrison for three years.
If five men are lost in battle,
or if five men die in battle and their bodies are not recovered,
all the merit of the members of the same group of five shall be taken away;
if their bodies are recovered,
all their crimes shall be pardoned.
The advantage or disadvantage of an army
lies in the reputation and reality of the state.
Now, reputation is in the government office, but reality is in the family.
The government office does not obtain the reality,
and the family does not obtain the reputation.
Assembling soldiers into an army
creates empty titles without substance,
Outsiders are insufficient to resist the enemy,
insiders are insufficient to defend the country;
this is why the army's supplies are not adequate,
and why the generals' authority is taken away.
Your subject believes that when soldiers flee and return,
their roommates and the low-ranking officers should be fined grain to increase supplies,
nominally for military provisions.
This creates the name of having one army,
but actually providing for two;
the country is emptied,
and the people are exhausted annually.
How can we avoid the disaster of fleeing north in defeat?
Now, using laws to stop desertion and return,
and prohibiting soldiers from running away from the army,
is the first victory of the army.
With groups of ten and five connecting,
and soldiers and officers helping each other in battle,
this is the second victory of the army.
If the general can establish authority,
and the soldiers can maintain discipline,
the commands are clear and trustworthy,
and both attack and defense are effective,
this is the third victory of the army.
Your subject has heard that those skilled in using soldiers in ancient times
could afford to lose half of their soldiers,
the next best could afford to lose one-third,
To kill eleven of those below him.
If he can kill half of them,
his authority will extend throughout the realm;
if he kills thirteen,
his power will be imposed upon the feudal lords;
if he kills eleven,
his commands will be carried out by the soldiers.
Therefore it is said:
a million men who do not follow orders are not as good as ten thousand men fighting;
ten thousand men fighting
wàn rén zhī dòu,
are not as good as a hundred men fighting fiercely.
Rewards should be like the sun and moon,
trustworthiness should be like the four seasons,
commands should be like axes and halberds,
sharpness should be like Gān Jiàng's sword,
if soldiers do not follow orders,
such a thing will not happen.
